propositions.text: Respondents are Romanian citizens who obtained refugee status in Canada on September 21, 2005.
propositions.quote: Respondents XXXX XXXX, XXXX XXXX, XXXX XXXX, XXXX XXXX and XXXX XXXX XXXX are citizens of Romania. They obtained refugee status in Canada on September 21, 2005.

propositions.text: Minister applies to determine respondents' refugee protection has ceased due to voluntary re-availment of Romanian protection.
propositions.quote: The Minister of Public Safety and Emergency Preparedness (hereinafter referred to as the Minister) is applying to the panel to determine that the respondents' refugee protection has ceased because the respondents voluntarily re-availed themselves of the protection of their country of nationality.

paragraphs.summary: Court states respondents are Romanian citizens granted refugee status in Canada; Minister applies to end their protection due to voluntary re-availment of Romanian protection.

propositions.text: Mother acted as designated representative for minor respondent during refugee and subsequent IRB proceedings.
propositions.quote: The mother, XXXX XXXX, acted as the designated representative for XXXX XXXX, who was 17 years of age on the day of the hearing.

propositions.text: Mother designated under subrule 20(6) of the Rules for refugee claim and all subsequent IRB proceedings.
propositions.quote: The mother was designated as such during the proceedings in respect of the refugee protection claim as well as for all subsequent proceedings before the Immigration and Refugee Board (IRB), as stipulated in subrule 20(6) of the Rules.

paragraphs.summary: Court states mother was designated representative for minor respondent during refugee claim and all IRB proceedings under subrule 20(6).

propositions.text: Respondents submitted Personal Information Forms alleging persecution due to Roma nationality.
propositions.quote: The respondents claimed refugee protection using a Personal Information Form (hereinafter referred to as the PIF), which they submitted to the IRB on May 13, 2005, and August 9, 2005. In their PIF, the respondents allege that they are victims of persecution in their country of origin by reason of their Roma nationality.

paragraphs.summary: Respondents allege persecution in Romania due to Roma nationality in their Personal Information Forms submitted to IRB.

propositions.text: IRB held hearing on September 7, 2005, and granted refugee protection on September 21, 2005.
propositions.quote: Their hearing before the IRB was held on September 7, 2005. On September 21, 2005, the IRB granted them refugee protection and established their status as Convention refugees.

paragraphs.summary: IRB held hearing and granted respondents refugee protection on September 21, 2005.

propositions.text: CBSA seized Romanian passports issued in 2008 for all five respondents via power of attorney.
propositions.quote: On April 14, 2010, the Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA) made a mail seizure and found the passports of the five respondents: Romanian passports issued on XXXX XXXX, 2008, for XXXX, on XXXX XXXX, 2008, for XXXX, on XXXX XXXX, 2008, for XXXX XXXX and on XXXX XXXX, 2008, for XXXX and XXXX. These passports were issued in Romania by means of a power of attorney signed by the respondents.

paragraphs.summary: CBSA seized Romanian passports issued in 2008 for respondents, obtained via power of attorney.

propositions.text: None of the respondents have permanent residence in Canada yet.
propositions.quote: None of the respondents have permanent residence in Canada yet.

paragraphs.summary: Court notes respondents do not yet have permanent residence in Canada.

propositions.text: Panel determines respondents' refugee protection has ceased due to voluntary re-availment of Romanian protection.
propositions.quote: Taking into account all the evidence on record, the panel determines that the respondents' refugee protection has ceased because they voluntarily re-availed themselves of the protection of their country of nationality, Romania.

paragraphs.summary: Panel determines respondents' refugee protection ceased due to voluntary re-availment of Romanian protection.

propositions.text: Minister sent notice of intervention on February 23, 2011; panel requested counsel name; mail returned twice to two addresses.
propositions.quote: On February 23, 2011, the Minister sent the respondents the notice of intervention for this hearing. The IRB received a copy of this notice on February 25, 2011. On March 4, 2011, the panel sent the respondents a letter asking them for the name of their counsel. The panel's mail was returned on two occasions, on March 17, 2011, and March 23, 2011. The mail was sent to two different addresses.

paragraphs.summary: Minister sent intervention notice; panel requested counsel name; mail returned twice to different addresses.

propositions.text: Panel sent notice to appear February 23, 2012; mail returned; new address found; postponements granted; hearing rescheduled to January 10, 2014.
propositions.quote: The panel sent a notice to appear, on February 23, 2012, the mail was returned. After receiving a new address found by the CBSA, on March 7, 2012, the panel sent another notice to appear on March 13, 2013. On March 22, 2012, the panel received a request for postponement from a counsel with respect to the hearing set for April 12, 2012. The request was granted. A new hearing date was scheduled for November 12, 2013. On October 29, 2013, a new counsel requested a postponement of the scheduled hearing. That request was granted. The hearing was scheduled for January 10, 2014.

paragraphs.summary: Panel sent notices; mail returned; new address found; postponements granted; hearing set for January 10, 2014.

propositions.text: On hearing day, some respondents attended; counsel requested postponement due to illness; postponement granted; absent respondents did not request postponement or alternate hearing.
propositions.quote: On the day of the hearing, some of the respondents attended, namely, XXXX, XXXX and XXXX. The counsel attended, but he requested a postponement because he was XXXX. The postponement was granted because of the counsel's XXXX XXXX. The panel asked the attending respondents where XXXX and XXXX XXXX were. XXXX stated that they were in Vancouver. The panel explained to the principal respondent that they would have to attend the next hearing, to be held on March 25, 2014. The panel gave them sufficient time to take the steps required to be able to attend in Montréal. At the March 25, 2014, hearing the panel noted that XXXX and XXXX XXXX were absent again. They did not request that the panel postpone the hearing or change the location or that they be heard by other means. As a result, the panel nevertheless proceeded with the hearing in the absence of those two respondents. In addition, the mother stated that she had sent them to Ireland and that she would look after their interests. Furthermore, the counsel in attendance was representing them.

paragraphs.summary: Some respondents attended hearing; counsel postponed due to illness; absent respondents did not request postponement; panel proceeded in their absence.

propositions.text: Minister applies to determine respondents' refugee protection ceased due to voluntary re-availment under IRPA paragraph 108(1)(a).
propositions.quote: In light of the evidence, the Minister is applying to the panel to determine that the respondents' refugee protection has ceased because they voluntarily re-availed themselves of the protection of their country of nationality, Romania, pursuant to paragraph 108(1)(a) of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act.

paragraphs.summary: Minister applies to panel to determine respondents' refugee protection ceased under IRPA paragraph 108(1)(a).

propositions.text: UNHCR Handbook articles 118-125 guide cessation; requires voluntary act, intention to re-avail, and actual protection obtained.
propositions.quote: The panel will refer to the Office of the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees Handbook for assistance in deciding this application; articles 118 to 125 deal with this clause. The clause implies three requirements to apply: the refugee must act voluntarily, he must intend by his action to re-avail himself of the protection of the country of his nationality, and he must actually obtain such protection.

propositions.text: UNHCR Handbook article 121 presumes intent to avail protection if refugee obtains national passport or renewal absent proof to contrary.
propositions.quote: In addition, according to article 121 of the Handbook: If a refugee applies for and obtains a national passport or its renewal, it will, in the absence of proof to the contrary, be presumed that he intends to avail himself of the protection of the country of his nationality.

paragraphs.summary: Court cites UNHCR Handbook requiring voluntary act, intent, and actual protection; passport issuance presumes intent to avail protection.

propositions.text: Respondents applied for Romanian passports to ease travel to Ireland, as refugee travel documents complicated travel.
propositions.quote: The respondents indicated through counsel in Exhibit M-7 that they applied for these passports to make it easier for them to travel to Ireland because, based on their explanations, travelling with a refugee travel document is complicated, as getting to Ireland directly is often difficult. Their Romanian passport makes it easier for them to travel.

paragraphs.summary: Respondents say they applied for Romanian passports to facilitate travel to Ireland due to refugee travel document difficulties.

propositions.text: Respondents acknowledged obtaining Romanian passports; principal respondent explained application during Ireland trip; passports used only to go to Ireland; passports left in Ireland.
propositions.quote: At the hearing, the respondents acknowledged that they applied for and obtained Romanian passports. The principal respondent explained that she applied for them during a trip to Ireland, the exact date of which she could no longer recall. She and her children-XXXX XXXX, XXXX (born in 1997) and XXXX-allegedly left Canada with a refugee travel document. They transited through Germany and, upon their arrival there, it was impossible for them to get to Ireland. At that point, she allegedly contacted a cousin in Romania and sent him a power of attorney so that he could obtain Romanian passports for her and her accompanying children, namely, XXXX XXXX, XXXX (born in 1997) and XXXX. They allegedly used them only to go to Ireland. She and her children allegedly left with their refugee travel documents and forgot all their Romanian passports in Ireland. The documents allegedly remained there in the principal respondent's purse. However, XXXX travelled to Ireland later, and the principal respondent took the same steps to obtain a passport for him.

paragraphs.summary: Respondents admit obtaining Romanian passports to travel to Ireland; allege passports left in Ireland; principal respondent explained process.

propositions.text: Panel finds respondents obtained passports voluntarily, not under force, to travel more easily to Ireland.
propositions.quote: With respect to the respondent's willingness, the panel is of the opinion that they obtained their passports voluntarily. The respondents were not forced to do so. They did so of their own accord in order to travel to Ireland more quickly and more easily.

paragraphs.summary: Panel finds respondents voluntarily obtained passports to facilitate travel to Ireland.

propositions.text: Panel finds respondents intended to use Romanian passports to travel to Ireland, not just for convenience.
propositions.quote: With respect to intention, the respondents alleged that they applied for their passports to make it easier for them to travel to Ireland. However, the panel notes that they chose to travel using a Romanian passport rather than their refugee travel document accompanied by the appropriate visa.

propositions.text: Respondents traveled to Germany with refugee travel document, then used Romanian passports to get to Ireland, showing knowledge and intent.
propositions.quote: In fact, they travelled to Germany using a refugee travel document, subsequently applied for a Romanian passport to get to Ireland, and left Ireland for Canada using their refugee travel documents.

propositions.text: Respondents were not obliged to use Romanian passports; could have obtained visas from Canadian authorities.
propositions.quote: The respondents were in no way obliged to use a Romanian passport to get to Ireland. They could have taken steps and obtained the visas required for their trip from Canadian authorities.

propositions.text: Panel does not believe respondents forgot passports in Ireland; passports were sent to Canada two years later after CBSA seizure.
propositions.quote: The panel also does not believe that the respondents forgot their Romanian passports in Ireland, because the respondents did not all travel together. XXXX returned to Canada from Ireland on XXXX XXXX, 2014. He left his passport in Ireland while the other respondents were still there. XXXX explained that, when she had travelled with XXXX, XXXX and XXXX XXXX on XXXX XXXX, she forgot the passports in Ireland. If the respondents had truly forgotten them, they would have asked a family member in Ireland to send them as quickly as possible. Instead, the passports were sent in XXXX 2010, nearly two years later. That is when the CBSA made the mail seizure.

propositions.text: Panel believes respondents wanted to hide from Canadian authorities that they had Romanian passports.
propositions.quote: The panel is of the opinion that the respondents wanted to hide from Canadian authorities the fact that they had applied for Romanian passports.

paragraphs.summary: Panel finds respondents intended to use Romanian passports to travel, did not forget them, and tried to hide possession from Canadian authorities.

propositions.text: Panel finds respondents intended to go to Romania, as refugee travel documents exclude travel to country of persecution.
propositions.quote: Given the lack of credibility and despite the fact that the respondents alleged that they did not travel to Romania using their Romanian passports, the panel is of the opinion that, on a balance of probabilities, the respondents' intention was to go to Romania, as the only reason for obtaining the passport was the fact that a refugee travel document allows an individual to travel anywhere, except to their country of persecution, in this case, Romania.

paragraphs.summary: Panel finds respondents intended to go to Romania, as refugee travel documents exclude travel to country of persecution.

propositions.text: Obtaining passports is evidence respondents obtained protection from Romania.
propositions.quote: The fact that they procured passports is evidence that they obtained protection. The passports for which they applied were issued to them.

paragraphs.summary: Panel finds obtaining passports evidences respondents obtained Romanian protection.

propositions.text: Respondents failed to rebut presumption they intended to re-avail themselves of Romanian protection by obtaining passports.
propositions.quote: For the above-mentioned reasons, the panel is of the opinion that the respondents failed to rebut the presumption that they wanted to re-avail themselves of the protection of their country of nationality by obtaining the passports.

propositions.text: This applies also to two minor respondents who were minors when passports issued; no evidence their intention differed from mother's.
propositions.quote: This also applies to the two respondents who did not attend the hearing, namely, XXXX and XXXX XXXX. They were minors when their passports were issued in 2008. However, it was not shown that their intention at that time was different from the intention of their mother, the principal respondent.

paragraphs.summary: Panel finds respondents failed to rebut presumption of intent to re-avail Romanian protection; applies to minor respondents too.

propositions.text: Minister discharged burden of proof; respondents voluntarily re-availed themselves of Romanian protection.
propositions.quote: The panel finds that the Minister discharged his burden of proof and that the respondents voluntarily re-availed themselves of the protection of their country of citizenship, Romania.

paragraphs.summary: Panel concludes Minister met burden; respondents voluntarily re-availed themselves of Romanian protection.

propositions.text: The panel allows the application to cease refugee protection filed by the Minister.
propositions.quote: the panel allows the application to cease refugee protection filed by the Minister of Public Safety and Emergency Preparedness.

propositions.text: The refugee protection of the respondents has ceased pursuant to subsection 108(2) of the IRPA.
propositions.quote: The panel determines that the refugee protection of the respondents has ceased pursuant to subsection 108(2) of the IRPA.

paragraphs.summary: The panel allows the Minister's application to cease refugee protection and finds protection ceased under IRPA s.108(2).

propositions.text: The refugee protection claims of the named respondents must be rejected.
propositions.quote: The refugee protection claims of XXXX XXXX, XXXX XXXX, XXXX XXXX, XXXX XXXX and XXXX XXXX XXXX must therefore be rejected.

propositions.text: The respondents are neither Convention refugees nor persons in need of protection.
propositions.quote: The respondents are neither "Convention refugees" nor "persons in need of protection"

propositions.text: The respondents voluntarily re-availed themselves of protection of Romania, their country of nationality.
propositions.quote: because they voluntarily re-availed themselves of the protection of their country of nationality, Romania.

paragraphs.summary: The panel rejects the respondents' claims, finding they voluntarily re-availed themselves of Romanian protection and are not refugees or protected persons.
